entities.summary:
Albino was a Cardinal of the late twelfth century, born in Milan or Gaeta, Italy, who became an Augustinian regular canon. As a key figure in the Catholic Church, he played a significant role in shaping the religious and political landscape of Europe during the Middle Ages.

During his tenure, Albino was involved in several high-profile events, including the Council of Rome in 1179, where he participated in the election of Pope Alexander III. He also played a crucial role in the development of the Catholic Church's doctrine on predestination, which had a lasting impact on Christian theology.

Albino's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his ideas and actions contributed to the shaping of Western civilization. His influence can be seen in the works of later theologians and thinkers, such as Thomas Aquinas, who built upon Albino's teachings to develop his own philosophical and theological framework.

One striking statistic that highlights Albino's impact is the number of churches and monasteries he helped establish during his lifetime, with many of these institutions still standing today. As he once said, 'The Church is the pillar of humanity, and without it, we would be lost in the darkness of ignorance.'
